title: crossworkload-kv-quantization-latency-regret-matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a cross-workload suite to quantify INT8 vs FP8 KV-cache quantization trade-offs and produce a latency-regret matrix that informs runtime precision switching rules. Goal: identify per-model, per-seqlen, per-batch regimes where INT8 yields acceptable quality with >25% latency/throughput gains vs FP8, and surface the operating thresholds for automatic precision switching to meet p95 latency SLOs without material quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Latency-regret matrix produced and stored as CSV + dashboard tile
Calibration pipeline documented and scripted (one-click run via calib-runner)
Switching policy prototype added to runtime with feature flag (canary)
At most 1% quality regression (delta-metric defined) in 'safe' INT8 regime across eval set
Bench harness reproducible: exact Docker + seed + dataset references in run logs
experiment_plan: Select 3 model families: Llama2-13B-32k, Mistral-7B, and an internal 70B candidate
Define workloads: short-chat (avg seqlen 64), mid-doc (512), long-context (4096)
Calib modes: per-layer symmetric, per-block asymmetric entropy, and runtime dynamic rescale (quick-iter)
Metrics: p95 latency (cold/hot), tokens/sec, throughput at fixed concurrency, perplexity on eval set, rouge/bleu delta for summarization/qa, and embedding cosine drift
Run matrix: for each model x workload x batchsize {1,4,8} x precision {FP8, INT8} x calibration mode
Collect KV cache memory footprint and GC/eviction rates under sustained load
Compute 'regret' = (relative quality drop) / (latency delta) and visualize as heatmaps
Annotate operating points where regret < threshold (safe to switch) and where latency SLOs require fallback to FP8
experimental_results_summary: Preliminary runs (2025-02-19): INT8 reduces average token latency by 22%-38% vs FP8 on Mistral-7B in mid-doc workload at batch 4, with average rouge drop of 0.6 points (0.9%).
Llama2-13B-32k long-context: FP8 still outperforms INT8 on quality for >2048 prefix lengths; INT8 brings 30% latency improvement for <1024 effective seqlen with negligible quality impact.
Internal-70B: INT8 calibration unstable under per-block asymmetric mode; introduced variance across seeds causing up to 3% perplexity regression — marking as 'needs further calibration'.
KV memory: INT8 reduces KV footprint by ~45% vs FP8, enabling higher batching at same GPU memory budget which translates to throughput wins in high concurrency scenarios.

Regret matrix outcome: identified 6 safe operating tiles (model x seqlen x batch) where INT8 is within 0.5% quality delta and yields >25% latency reduction — these are candidates for default runtime switch with a conservative fallback policy.
detailed_notes: Calibration approach that performed best: two-phase pipeline: offline per-layer symmetric scaling initialized by layer activation stats + lightweight runtime dynamic scale smoothing (exponential moving average with alpha=0.2).

For Mistral-7B, blockwise asymmetric with entropy objective gave lowest perplexity but required much larger calibration set (10k sequences) to stabilize — heavier compute cost for calibration compared to symmetric per-layer.

We observed quantization-induced attention head noise manifested as sporadic token hallucination in long-context completion. Mitigation: introduce KV-correction pass that re-reads last T tokens in FP16 before emitting when confidence metric falls below threshold.

Runtime switching policy: predicted p95 latency based on current queue length and active batching; if predicted > SLO and safe-tile flag true then switch to INT8 for new requests; otherwise keep FP8. Implemented as feature-flagged policy in branch runtime/feat/precision-switch.
Bench harness: Docker image ghcr.io/redwood/kv-quant-bench:20250218 + seed 42 + dataset refs in links below. All runs stored in s3://redwood-inference-experiments/kv-quant/eng-99642/.

Quality delta definition: for chat/summarize tasks we use composite delta = max(normalized-perplexity-delta, normalized-rouge-delta) to conservatively capture regressions across tasks. Threshold for 'safe' set to 0.5% composite delta.

Edge case: under multi-tenant bursty traffic patterns, switching cost (model reconfigure + kernel warmup) incurred a 1.8x transient latency spike for first few tokens. Solution: pre-warm INT8 kernels under predicted load via predictive prefetch in next iteration.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration datasets may not reflect real customer distributions leading to undetected regressions. Mitigation: incorporate sampled anonymized customer prompts into calibration corpus and run closed-loop evals where allowed.
Risk: Kernel warmup cost when switching precision may violate short SLO windows. Mitigation: implement kernel pre-warm heuristics and include warmup latency in cost model used by switching policy.

Risk: INT8 instabilities on very deep models (70B+) could introduce intermittent quality issues. Mitigation: default to FP8 for flagged models and invest in per-layer bias-correction in the calibration pipeline.

Risk: Operational complexity of many per-tenant precision profiles. Mitigation: group tenants into buckets by workload pattern and use shared profiles; add console UX for visibility and manual overrides.
